tess: Quick note — after the CUDA kernel swap from r12 to r13 we have a consistent ~18% tail-latency regression on Mistral-7B FP8 AWQ runs and a small accuracy delta on the calibration set. repro + profile below. anyone seen head-wise quant noise like this? :thinking:

omar: Can you paste the perf numbers and the exact command to repro?

jade: tagging here because kernel selection fallback logic might be involved. r13 changed block GEMM tiling on small heads.

sasha: repro'd locally. baseline (r12, AWQ): p50 80ms / p95 210ms / p99 380ms. after r13 (AWQ FP8 path): p50 92ms / p95 252ms / p99 450ms. accuracy (calib prompts): top1 drop ~0.9% absolute on the evaluation slice (8 prompts).

mike: interesting — is GPTQ path affected the same way? could be kernel schedule swap for head dims that triggers suboptimal microkernel.

ash: (not in thread) fwiw FP8 kernels call a different vectorized path when head_dim % 16 == 0 — might trigger different ldg/stg patterns.

omar: I bisected quickly. suspect commit 9f3a2b4 (cuda: optimize small-GEMM tiling) flips kernel for head_dim 64/80/128. when we force fallback to legacy kernel p95/p99 return to baseline.

sasha: repro command (docker runtime):
```
# minimal repro
python -m infra.run_infer \
  --model=mistral-7b-awq-fp8 \
  --batch=8 \
  --seq=512 \
  --profile=flame --iters=200
```
Attached flame sample: hot loop is in gemm_small_optimized (r13). fallback path gemm_legacy is ~1.2x faster for these shapes.

jade: This smells like kernel selection heuristic needs an extra shape/seq-awareness. Batching heuristics also matter — continuous batching grouped by seq-length bins could reduce the impact because the optimized kernel has higher setup cost but better steady throughput at long seqs.

mike: For immediate mitigation we can: 1) add temporary kernel-fallback for AWQ FP8 on head_dims <= 128; 2) adjust dynamic-batcher to prefer grouping by seq-length (bins 64/128/256/512) instead of pure arrival time; 3) relax KV eviction aggressiveness to avoid extra refills that amplify tail spikes.

tess: I ran an experiment toggling KV eviction threshold from 0.6 -> 0.8: p95 dropped ~9% (252 -> 230ms) on r13+fallback. suggests case where eviction churn plus heavier kernel setup causes cascaded tail.

omar: Good data. Can we get a quick kernel feature-flag to fallback for the affected shapes and add an integration test that runs the 8-calib prompts and checks accuracy delta < 0.5%?

sasha: created branch: runtime/fp8-kernel-fallback-189876 — patch toggles kernel when (model_family=="mistral" && quant=="awq" && head_dim <= 128). Ran canary: p50 85ms / p95 218ms / p99 385ms, accuracy back to baseline within noise.

infra-bot: deploy request queued for runtime/fp8-kernel-fallback-189876 by sasha — env=staging, sha=6a7b2c.

ci-bot: perf-regression-checker: running nightly perf tests for mistral-7b-awq-fp8 (canary).

jade: longer term we should: - incorporate RoPE scaling check in eval (we saw slight increase in hallucination score when mixing FP8+rope-scale>1.0) - add head-dim aware kernel cost model to kernel selector - extend dynamic batcher to do seq-length bucketing and prefer coalescing small heads together to amortize kernel setup.

mike: Agreed. Also add a small microbenchmark for FP8 vs INT8 kernel choice to the kernel CI so future tiling changes trigger alerts.

tess: thanks everyone. next actions: sasha push canary, mike open kernel-selector ticket with perf model, jade draft batcher change PR, omar add CI microbench. I'll drop the calibration prompt set and flame tarball in the thread files. :thumbsup:

sasha: uploaded artifacts -> gs://redwood-perf/mistral/1898765432/{flame.tar.gz,calib_prompts.json,perf.csv}
